items.title: Intrepid’s Co-Founder Wants Travelers Closer to Home
items.summary: Intrepid thinks U.S. customers can swap Morocco for New Mexico to bring down flight emissions. The result: a test of whether culture and connection matter more to travelers than distance.

items.title: Capital Allocation: How Should Travel Invest in Its Future?
items.summary: Physical assets, curated experiences, and trained human expertise are the most durable investments because AI makes them more valuable.

items.title: How to Plan for an Uncertain Future
items.summary: Every global hospitality company is deciding whether to optimize for margin or for reach. Accor is choosing reach.

items.title: Rethinking Impact and Sustainable Frameworks That Scale
items.summary: Every hospitality company has a sustainability commitment. Most of them sit in a report.

items.title: Transforming Travel’s Future
items.summary: The Forum spent two days measuring the value of the traveler. Prince Harry asked whether anyone is measuring the health of the destination.

items.title: Permission to Exist: Rethinking the Role of the Industry
items.summary: Travel companies are trying to turn loyalty programs into a membership. Chenault built the model they’re copying.

items.title: How to Build for Travel’s Agentic Future
items.summary: Almost every travel brand CEO at Skift Global Forum touched on what they want AI agents to do. Fewer talked about how they expect it to work.

items.title: Rebuilding as an AI-Native Company
items.summary: Many travel companies are deciding whether to layer AI onto their existing business or rebuild around it. Chesky chose to rebuild.
